title: Start from the pattern library, not the page
principle: Frost’s Pattern Lab lineage (Atomic Design ch.3–4, public): effective systems expose patterns in isolation and in context. When prompting AI, seed with the library’s patterns first so pages inherit, rather than reverse-engineering a library from a pretty page.
procedure: Open or sketch the pattern inventory before net-new screens.
Prompt AI to assemble from named patterns; forbid silent new primitives.
Toggle patterns through states (default/hover/disabled) in isolation.
Only then compose a page and note which patterns were missing—and promote them.
examplePrompts: Assemble this screen ONLY from our pattern list: [paste]. If a need isn’t covered, propose a pattern addition—don’t silently invent. Cite Atomic Design / Pattern Lab workflow.
Generate isolation stories for Button / Field / Card (default, hover, error, disabled) before any marketing page.
promptWhy: Forbids silent invention—the main AI systems failure.
Isolation stories catch state gaps early.
tips: Tool-agnostic: Pattern Lab is illustrative, not required.

workedExamples.title: Page-first debt
workedExamples.before: AI ships a gorgeous settings page with unique toggles.
workedExamples.after: Extract Toggle pattern; rebuild page from library.

workedExamples.title: Missing error state
workedExamples.body: Isolation story reveals Field never had error—caught before QA.

antiPatterns: Pattern docs that omit interactive states.
checklist: Pattern inventory referenced in the prompt.
New needs proposed as patterns, not one-offs.
